Fever, red-brown/"redwater" urine (blood in urine), anaemia, weakness, loss of appetite

High fever, nervous signs (circling, muscle tremors, pushing head against objects, aggression or anxious behaviour), can progress rapidly to death — mortality up to 90% in susceptible animals if untreated
General tick control guidance (applies across B1–B4)

Variable, but commonly: respiratory distress (gasping, coughing), greenish watery diarrhea, drop in egg production and/or thin-shelled misshapen eggs, and in later stages nervous signs (twisted neck/head, paralysis, tremors). Sudden deaths with few warning signs are common in unvaccinated flocks
my chickens are having difficulty breathing
Coughing, sneezing, nasal discharge, watery eyes, reduced egg production, and in laying birds, misshapen or poor-quality eggshells. Generally lower mortality than ND but can be severe in young chicks

Bloody or watery diarrhea, ruffled feathers, lethargy, pale comb/wattles (anemia), reduced growth in young birds, huddling. Birds under 10-14 days old are generally not yet susceptible; risk rises as chicks start actively pecking at litter
In young chicks: diarrhea, weakness, high mortality. In adult birds (fowl typhoid specifically): depression, pale comb, reduced appetite, greenish-yellow diarrhea, sudden deaths

fever, firm raised skin nodules/lumps, enlarged lymph nodes, swelling of limbs or brisket, eye/nose discharge, reduced milk production, weakness, and sometimes skin lesions that become damaged or infected
fever, excessive salivation/drooling, blisters or erosions in the mouth/tongue, sores around the feet/coronary band, lameness, reluctance to move, and sudden drop in milk
sudden death, fever before death, bleeding/discharge from body openings, rapidly bloating carcass, and lack of normal rigor mortis can occur, but signs are not always complete
sudden lameness, fever, painful swelling of large muscles, depression, and rapid death. Swellings can later feel crackly because of gas
swollen, hot, painful udder quarter; abnormal milk with flakes, clots, watery appearance or blood; reduced milk; fever or weakness in severe cases
sunken eyes, dry mouth, weakness, inability to suck, cold ears/ legs, inability to stand, or blood in stool
coughing, rapid/laboured breathing, nasal discharge, fever, poor appetite, depression
depression, ruffled feathers, watery diarrhea, vent pecking, trembling, dehydration, and sudden increase in mortality
scabby lesions on comb, wattles, eyelids or unfeathered skin ("dry" form), or lesions in the mouth/upper respiratory tract ("wet" form)
panting, wings held away from body, crowding near water, reduced feed intake, reduced egg production, weakness, death in severe heat
narrow pale/yellow streaks running along leaves; plants infected when young may become severely stunted and produce little grain
long rectangular grey/tan lesions often restricted by leaf veins; lesions can merge and dry large areas of leaf
holes in leaves, "dead heart" in young plants, tunneling inside stems, weak/broken stems, frass near entry holes, poor cob development
rapidly expanding water-soaked/dark lesions on leaves and stems; white growth may appear at lesion edges under humid conditions; fruit can develop firm brown lesions
mines/blotches in leaves, galleries in stems, pinholes and tunneling in fruit; small larvae may be found within mines
clusters of small soft-bodied insects on tender shoots/undersides of leaves, curling/distortion, sticky honeydew, sometimes black sooty mould
tiny white insects fly from leaf undersides when disturbed; nymphs remain attached underneath leaves; honeydew and sooty mould can develop
